rationale: Compound ⲙⲛⲧ- (abstract prefix) + ϫⲛⲁ (Sahidic 'force') + ⲛ̄ⲥ- = 'state of forcing-against.' Standard Coptic abstract for 'violence, oppression.' Used here in a legal-judicial sense paralleling ⲁⲛⲟⲙⲓⲁ 'lawlessness.'
Greek loanword ἀνομία. Standard biblical-legal term.
Greek loanword συναγωγή. Here referring to the judicial council that condemned Jesus.
Greek-derived verb τάσσω. Used twice here: ⲁⲩⲧⲁⲝⲁϥ 'they appointed/sentenced him' (line 2, judicial sense) and ⲁϥⲧⲁⲝⲣⲁⲩ 'he established them' (line 21, ecclesiastical sense).
Greek loanword λῃστής. The Synoptic crucifixion narrative term.
Greek loanword τάφος. Standard burial term.
Greek loanword σκανδαλίζω. The fall-into-error sense fits the historiographical context of post-apostolic decline.
Greek loanword δίκαιος ('righteous') + Coptic ⲣⲙ̄ⲙⲏⲉ ('men of truth'). Stock Manichaean designation for the post-apostolic tradition-keepers, paralleling the apostles in role.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲗⲱϫϫ 'narrow, constrained.' Qualitative form. Matthean contrast with ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'wide' confirms reading.
Qualitative of ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲧⲛ 'be wide, spread.' Matthean 'broad way' (Matt 7:13).
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲱϫⲛ 'fail, come to end.' Used of institutional decline.
Lycopolitan ⲥⲱⲝⲧ̄ = Sahidic ⲥⲱϣⲧ̄ 'turn aside' + ⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ 'backward.' Spatial-temporal regression.
Greek loanword χωρίς 'without, apart from.' Standard.
ⲥⲛⲩ = Lycopolitan ⲥⲙⲟⲧ 'form, fashion, manner' with demonstrative ⲡⲓ-. The repeated ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ ⲁⲛ = 'in this same manner again,' signaling typological parallel.

proposed_english: be put to shame / suffer disgrace
rationale: ⲣ̄- + ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ = 'do/enter the shame-state.' Standard Coptic verbal compound for αἰσχύνεσθαι.
